analysis: The code snippet contains two calls to String.substring within the 'if (line.contains(" "))' block. The first call is line.substring(0, line.indexOf(" ")). Since line.contains(" ") is true, line.indexOf(" ") returns a non-negative integer less than the length of the string. Thus beginIndex is 0 (valid) and endIndex is within bounds (0 <= endIndex <= length). No IndexOutOfBoundsException is thrown. The second call is line.substring(line.indexOf(" ") + 1). Again, because line.contains(" ") is true, the index is at least 0, so beginIndex is at least 1. The highest possible value is line.length() (if the space is at the last character), which is allowed. Thus beginIndex is never negative nor greater than the length, so no exception. Both calls are safely guarded by the condition, so all throwing conditions of IndexOutOfBoundsException are avoided.
